title: For k at most n, truncating a type to n and then to k is the same as truncating it to k
author: The Univalent Foundations Program

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source lines 743-746: for k at most n the iterated truncation collapses. The proof (source lines 747-764) is short but supplies the whole equivalence rather than a pointer: it defines the two maps by the recursion principle for truncations, verifies that each is well defined from the truncation level of its target (for the first one the level is exactly the hypothesis k at most n), and then checks both composites on the generating projections. The construction of the maps and the well-definedness checks are the substance and none of them is visible in the statement.
